Outcome_variable.evidence_source: [/page/5/Text/18] In the present study, we investigated change in the associations among the three basic psychological need satisfaction components (autonomy, relatedness, and competence) and well-being during the retirement transition. [/page/5/Text/19] We found that satisfaction of all three needs was positively related to well-being at the within-person level. These effects are [/page/6/Text/6] in line with previous research on the basic psychological needs (Ng et al., 2012; Reis et al., 2000; Sheldon et al., 1996) and confirm that need satisfaction is important for individual well-being.
Outcome_variable.warning: The paper uses the general term 'well-being' without specifying a particular measure (e.g., SWLS, PANAS). 'Life satisfaction' is inferred as the most general and common component of SWB when 'well-being' is used broadly in this context.
